scope: Same-host exact-token p512/p1024/p4096 prefill plus 128 post-first-output AR transitions; BF16 K/V; four categories; one warmup and three counterbalanced measured requests per case

protocol.classification: three-repeat counterbalanced screening; not the five-pair section-6 closure protocol

pristine_upstream_hip.decision: No pristine upstream HIP timing retained; patched-upstream HIP is separate and cannot be labeled stock.

nathan_identical_prompt.verdict: same-prompt nondeterministic; full-matrix rates are non-binding diagnostics

limitations: This is the three-repeat screening protocol, not section-6 closure: no five counterbalanced pairs or paired 95% confidence interval was collected.
Several per-row and repetition coefficients of variation exceed 2%; those rows are noisy rather than match/loss closure evidence.
Warm OS page-cache state was used. A separately isolated cold-PLE mode and category heldouts remain open P0 requirements.
Nathan Vulkan is same-prompt nondeterministic (16 unique outputs from 16 identical requests) and is excluded from repeatability-valid targets.
EngramHalo p4096 code output alternates between two hashes and is excluded from the repeatability-valid p4096 HIP target; its p512/p1024 shapes repeat exactly.
Pristine upstream HIP produced zero samples after two 1800-second starts. The measured patched-upstream HIP lane is explicitly non-stock.
Cross-engine generated-ID equality is diagnostic for production arithmetic; hipEngine binding quality remains governed by its calibrated execution-profile gates.

decision.retain_as: canonical exact-token screening baseline and implementation target map
decision.next: Use the repeatability-valid HIP/Vulkan screening rows to rank P1 work; do not promote Nathan or EngramHalo p4096 rates as correctness-valid closure targets.
